question: Non-Tax revenue is part of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue Receipts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Government receipts are classified into Revenue Receipts and Capital Receipts. Revenue Receipts are further divided into Tax Revenue and Non-Tax Revenue. (गैर-कर राजस्व — राजस्व प्राप्तियां)

 

• Tax Revenue includes receipts from taxes such as income tax, corporation tax, GST, customs and excise duties.

 

• Non-Tax Revenue includes interest receipts, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings, fees, fines, and receipts from general, social and economic services provided by the government.

 

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce any asset of the government, unlike capital receipts (e.g., borrowings, disinvestment proceeds).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Capital Receipts include loans raised by the government (market borrowings), recovery of loans, and proceeds from disinvestment of public sector assets.

 

• The Union Budget of India classifies all receipts under the Consolidated Fund of India into Revenue Account and Capital Account.

 

NOTE

 

• Revenue Expenditure (Option 1): This refers to expenditure that neither creates assets nor reduces liabilities, such as salaries, subsidies and interest payments — it is unrelated to non-tax revenue classification.

 

• Capital Expenditure (Option 3): This is expenditure incurred on acquiring assets or reducing liabilities, such as infrastructure creation and loan repayment.

 

• Capital Receipts (Option 4): These are receipts that create a liability or reduce assets, such as borrowings and disinvestment, not related to non-tax revenue.

question: In which Biosphere Reserve is the largest endangered marine mammal Dugong i.e., Dugong dugon and sea turtles also found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, located between India and Sri Lanka off the coast of Tamil Nadu, was India's first marine biosphere reserve, notified in 1989. (मन्नार की खाड़ी जैवमंडल रिज़र्व — डुगोंग व समुद्री कछुए)

 

• It is home to the largest population of the endangered marine mammal Dugong (Dugong dugon), also called the "sea cow", along with sea turtles, dolphins, and extensive coral reefs.

 

• It comprises 21 islands and covers a coastline of about 140 km, encompassing coral reefs, seagrass beds, mangroves and beaches between Rameswaram and Tuticorin.

 

• It was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and is part of the Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamil Nadu is home to the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park at the core of this biosphere reserve, specifically renowned for dugong conservation.

 

• India has designated multiple biosphere reserves; the Gulf of Mannar remains one of the few primarily marine in character among the earliest notified reserves.

 

NOTE

 

• Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve (Option 1): Located in Sikkim, known for high-altitude Himalayan flora and fauna including the snow leopard and red panda, not marine species.

 

• Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve (Option 2): Located in Andhra Pradesh, famous for Red Sanders (Red Sandalwood) forests, not a marine habitat.

 

• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve (Option 3): Located in Madhya Pradesh, a hill station biosphere reserve known for sal and bamboo forests, unrelated to dugongs.

question: Which year census is the 15th National census survey conducted by the Census Organisation of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2011.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years, and the 2011 Census was the 15th census in the decennial series, and the 7th after independence. (जनगणना 2011 — पंद्रहवीं जनगणना)

 

• The first synchronous census of India was conducted in 1881, and counting has continued uninterrupted every decade since then, making 2011 the fifteenth in this unbroken series (1881, 1891, 1901, ... 2011).

 

• The 2011 Census was conducted in two phases — House-listing and Housing Census, followed by Population Enumeration — under the Ministry of Home Affairs' Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.

 

• The theme/slogan associated with Census 2011 was "Our Census, Our future".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first census attempt in India, in 1872, is termed a non-synchronous census as it was not conducted at one point in time across the country.

 

• Census 2021 was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, so 2011 remains the most recent completed census.

 

NOTE

 

• 1991 (Option 1): This was the 13th census in the decennial series, not the 15th.

 

• 2001 (Option 2): This was the 14th census in the decennial series.

 

• 1981 (Option 3): This was the 12th census in the decennial series.

question: Which of the following is the only rack railway in India that was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nilgiri Mountain Railway, a metre-gauge rack railway connecting Mettupalayam to Udagamandalam (Ooty) in Tamil Nadu, was added as an extension to the "Mountain Railways of India" UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005. (नीलगिरी माउंटन रेलवे — रैक रेलवे, यूनेस्को धरोहर 2005)

 

• It is India's only rack railway, using the Abt rack and pinion system to climb steep gradients through the Nilgiri Hills, built by the British and opened in 1908.

 

• The "Mountain Railways of India" UNESCO group originally included only the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (inscribed in 1999); the Nilgiri Mountain Railway was added in 2005, and the Kalka–Shimla Railway was added later in 2008.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• These three railways are collectively recognised by UNESCO for their engineering ingenuity in navigating difficult mountainous terrain.

 

• The Nilgiri Mountain Railway operates over a track length of about 46 km, with the steepest section using the rack-and-pinion mechanism between Mettupalayam and Coonoor.

 

NOTE

 

• Kangra Valley Railway (Option 2): A narrow-gauge railway in Himachal Pradesh; it is not part of the UNESCO Mountain Railways of India group and is not a rack railway.

 

• Matheran Hill Railway (Option 3): A narrow-gauge heritage railway in Maharashtra, but not UNESCO-listed and not a rack railway.

 

• Kalka–Shimla Railway (Option 4): UNESCO-listed, but added in 2008, not 2005, and it operates on the adhesion system, not the rack (rack-and-pinion) system.

question: In which of the following sports, apart from volleyball, do players make use of the Screen technique?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "screen" (or pick) is an offensive technique used in basketball, where an offensive player positions themselves to block or "screen" a defender guarding a teammate, freeing that teammate to shoot, pass, or drive to the basket. (स्क्रीन तकनीक — बास्केटबॉल)

 

• Like volleyball, where a "screen" refers to blocking the opposing team's view of the server, basketball also uses the term to denote a legal offensive obstruction technique.

 

• A "screen" or "pick" is a core part of pick-and-roll offensive plays, a fundamental strategy in modern basketball.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In volleyball, a "screen" is actually an illegal tactic where players block the receiving team's view of the server — this is penalised as a fault, unlike in basketball where it is a legitimate offensive strategy.

 

• Common basketball screening techniques include the pick-and-roll and pick-and-pop.

 

NOTE

 

• Cricket (Option 2): The term "screen" in cricket refers to the sight screen, a piece of equipment placed behind the bowler's arm — it is not a playing technique used by players themselves.

 

• Baseball (Option 3): Does not use the screen technique; it revolves around pitching, batting and fielding positions.

 

• Handball (Option 4): Does not use the term "screen" as an official playing technique the way basketball does.

question: Which player led India at the women's Hockey Asia Cup in Muscat, which was held in January 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savita Punia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Savita Punia, India's goalkeeper, captained the Indian women's hockey team at the Women's Hockey Asia Cup 2022, held in Muscat, Oman, in January 2022. (सविता पूनिया — भारतीय महिला हॉकी टीम की कप्तान)

 

• Under her captaincy, India won the gold medal at the tournament, beating China in the final via a penalty shoot-out after the regulation match ended goalless.

 

• This victory ended a long wait for a major hockey title for the Indian women's team and boosted the side's confidence and ranking ahead of future international events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The men's and women's Hockey Asia Cup tournaments are organised separately by the Asian Hockey Federation.

 

• Savita Punia was later honoured with the Arjuna Award for her contributions to Indian hockey.

 

NOTE

 

• Navneet Kaur (Option 1): A forward on the Indian women's hockey team, but she was not the captain for this tournament.

 

• Rani Rampal (Option 2): A former captain of the Indian women's hockey team (led the side at the Tokyo Olympics 2020), but she was not the captain at the 2022 Asia Cup.

 

• Susmita Patil (Option 3): A member of the Indian women's hockey team, but not the team's captain for this tournament.

question: In how many agro-climatic zones has Tamil Nadu been classified?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu has been classified into seven agro-climatic zones by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), based on rainfall, soil type, cropping pattern and irrigation sources. (तमिलनाडु — सात कृषि-जलवायु क्षेत्र)

 

• These seven zones are: Cauvery Delta Zone, North Eastern Zone, North Western Zone, Western Zone, Southern Zone, High Rainfall Zone, and High Altitude Hilly Zone.

 

• Agro-climatic zoning helps in planning region-specific agricultural strategies, crop selection, and resource allocation for optimum productivity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the national level, the Planning Commission of India divided the whole country into 15 broad agro-climatic zones for macro-level agricultural planning.

 

• The Cauvery Delta Zone of Tamil Nadu is often called the "Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu" due to its high paddy productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• 3 (Option 1): Incorrect; this understates the number of officially recognised zones in Tamil Nadu.

 

• 9 (Option 2): Incorrect; this does not match the standard TNAU classification of Tamil Nadu.

 

• 5 (Option 4): Incorrect; this also does not match the standard classification of seven zones.

question: The President of India ___________ inaugurated Sangeet Natak Academi on 28 January 1953.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajendra Prasad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, was inaugurated by the first President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, on 28 January 1953 in New Delhi. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी — डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद)

 

• It is the oldest of the three National Akademis of Arts established by the Government of India, the other two being the Sahitya Akademi (literature) and the Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts).

 

• The Akademi confers prestigious annual honours such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Ratna and Akademi Puraskar) for outstanding contributions to Indian performing arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• It also administers affiliated institutions such as the Kathak Kendra and the National School of Drama.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (Option 1): He was the second President of India (1962-1967), but he was not President when the Akademi was inaugurated in 1953.

 

• Mohammad Hidayatullah (Option 2): He served as Chief Justice of India and later as Vice-President of India, not as President at the time of the Akademi's inauguration.

 

• Zakir Husain (Option 4): He became the third President of India in 1967, well after the Akademi's inauguration in 1953.

question: In which year did Walther Flemming coined the term 'chromatin' for the stained substance found in the cell nucleus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1879.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Walther Flemming, a German biologist, coined the term "chromatin" in 1879 to describe the readily-stainable substance found within the cell nucleus. (क्रोमैटिन — वाल्टर फ्लेमिंग, 1879)

 

• He is regarded as one of the founders of cytogenetics, and his work laid the foundation for understanding cell division, particularly mitosis, a term he also coined.

 

• Flemming used aniline dyes to stain cell nuclei and observed thread-like structures within — later termed chromosomes by Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz in 1888.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Flemming's landmark work, "Zellsubstanz, Kern und Zelltheilung" (1882), documented his detailed observations on cell division and chromatin behaviour.

 

• Chromatin consists of DNA tightly coiled around histone proteins, and it condenses into visible chromosomes during cell division.

 

NOTE

 

• 1900 (Option 1): Incorrect; this year is often associated with the rediscovery of Mendel's laws of inheritance, not Flemming's coining of "chromatin".

 

• 1840 (Option 2): Incorrect; this predates Flemming's work by decades.

 

• 1849 (Option 3): Incorrect; this also predates Flemming's actual discovery period by about three decades.

question: In which of the following Indian states, is Makar Sankranti celebrated by the name of 'Magha Saaji'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Himachal Pradesh, the festival of Makar Sankranti is celebrated as "Magha Saaji" (Maghi Saaji), marking the onset of the month of Magha and the start of the harvest season. (माघ साजी — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• The festival is celebrated with rituals of holy dips in rivers, community feasts, and offerings, symbolising the sun's transition (Sankranti) into the Capricorn (Makar) zodiac sign.

 

• Different regions of India celebrate Makar Sankranti under various regional names — this diversity in nomenclature is frequently tested in general awareness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Makar Sankranti is known as Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Lohri (a related festival) in Punjab, Bhogali Bihu in Assam, and Uttarayan in Gujarat.

 

• The festival is one of the few Hindu festivals that follows the solar calendar, and hence falls on a fixed date, usually 14 January, every year.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Here, the associated harvest festival is called Lohri, celebrated a day before Makar Sankranti, not "Magha Saaji".

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Makar Sankranti is celebrated here as "Ghughutia" or "Kale Kauva", not "Magha Saaji".

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): The festival is locally celebrated as "Tusu Parab", not by the name "Magha Saaji".

question: Who among the following was the flag bearer of the Indian contingent at the opening ceremony of the Asian Games 2018?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neeraj Chopra, the javelin thrower, was the flag bearer for the Indian contingent at the opening ceremony of the 2018 Asian Games held in Jakarta-Palembang, Indonesia. (नीरज चोपड़ा — 2018 एशियाई खेल ध्वजवाहक)

 

• He went on to win the gold medal in the men's javelin throw event at these very Games, cementing his stature in Indian athletics.

 

• The 2018 Asian Games were the 18th edition, and India finished with its best-ever medal tally at the time (69 medals: 15 gold, 24 silver, 30 bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra later won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics at the Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021) in the javelin throw event.

 

• He also won gold at the World Athletics Championships 2023 in Budapest.

 

NOTE

 

• Saina Nehwal (Option 2): An Indian badminton player who has represented India at multiple Asian Games and Olympics, but was not the flag bearer at the 2018 Asian Games opening ceremony.

 

• Bajrang Punia (Option 3): An Indian wrestler who won a medal at the 2018 Asian Games, but did not serve as India's flag bearer at the opening ceremony.

 

• PT Usha (Option 4): A legendary Indian sprinter of an earlier era; she did not carry the flag at the 2018 Asian Games opening ceremony.

question: Which is the largest Dun formations in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dehra Dun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Dun" refers to a longitudinal valley formation found between the Shiwalik Hills (Outer Himalayas) and the Lesser (Middle) Himalayas, and Dehra Dun, located in Uttarakhand, is the largest such Dun formation in India. (देहरादून — भारत का सबसे बड़ा दून)

 

• Dehra Dun lies between the Shiwalik range to the south and the Himalayan foothills to the north, and is drained by the rivers Ganga and Yamuna.

 

• Dehra Dun is the capital of Uttarakhand and is known for its pleasant climate, forests, and premier research and educational institutions such as the Forest Research Institute (FRI) and the Indian Military Academy (IMA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other, much smaller Dun formations exist in the Himalayan region, such as at Nalagarh and Kota.

 

• The Shiwalik range, also known as the Outer Himalayas, is the youngest and southernmost of the Himalayan ranges.

 

NOTE

 

• Harike Dun (Option 1): Not a recognised or notable Dun formation; "Harike" is better known as a wetland/wildlife sanctuary (Harike Wetland) in Punjab, unrelated to Himalayan Dun valleys.

 

• Nalagarh Dun (Option 2): A smaller Dun formation located in Himachal Pradesh, much less extensive than Dehra Dun.

 

• Kota Dun (Option 3): A relatively small Dun formation; "Kota" is more prominently known as a city in Rajasthan, unrelated to the largest Dun formation.

question: What do you understand by 'dual citizenship' as in the case of the US?
option_1: Citizenship of two states simultaneously with two countries
option_2: Citizenship of a country alongwith that of a constituent State, where one resides/born
option_3: Citizenship of two states alongwith two countries
solution_text:
The correct answer is Citizenship of a country alongwith that of a constituent State, where one resides/born.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In federal countries like the USA, citizens hold a form of "dual citizenship" — they are simultaneously citizens of the entire nation (federal/national citizenship) and citizens of the constituent State in which they reside or were born. (दोहरी नागरिकता — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका मॉडल)

 

• This differs from "dual citizenship" in the popular sense of holding passports of two different sovereign countries; here, it specifically means dual layers of citizenship within a single federal nation (national + state).

 

• India, in contrast, follows a single citizenship system under the Constitution — there is only Indian citizenship, with no separate state citizenship, even though India has a federal structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of dual citizenship (national and state) exists in federations such as the USA and Switzerland, whereas India, Canada, and Australia largely follow single citizenship despite being federal in structure.

 

• The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship (Articles 5-11) to promote unity and avoid discrimination on the basis of the state of residence or birth.

 

NOTE

 

• Citizenship of two states simultaneously with two countries (Option 1): This describes an inconsistent combination that does not correctly define the US model of dual citizenship.

 

• Citizenship of two states alongwith two countries (Option 3): This also incorrectly implies citizenship of two countries and two states together, which is not the standard definition being asked about.

 

• Citizenship of two countries simultaneously (Option 4): This describes the popular/international sense of dual citizenship (holding two nationalities), not the specific US federal-and-state sense being asked about here.

question: The first phase of the Green Revolution was restricted largely to two crops and the regions where they are grown. Which of the following pairs best represents these two crops?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat, rice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first phase of the Green Revolution in India (roughly mid-1960s to 1980s) was largely restricted to the introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds of wheat and rice, particularly in resource-rich regions like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh. (हरित क्रांति का प्रथम चरण — गेहूं व चावल)

 

• The revolution was spearheaded under the guidance of agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, often called the "Father of the Green Revolution in India", building on Norman Borlaug's HYV wheat varieties.

 

• Wheat production saw the most dramatic early gains due to its greater responsiveness to fertiliser and irrigation, with rice following closely as HYV rice seeds were introduced in irrigated tracts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The second phase (post-1980s) of the Green Revolution extended HYV technology to a wider range of crops and regions, including eastern India and crops like pulses and oilseeds.

 

• Excessive focus on wheat and rice monocultures in the first phase led to concerns about groundwater depletion and soil degradation in states like Punjab and Haryana.

 

NOTE

 

• Rice, corn (Option 1): Incorrect; corn (maize) was not among the two principal crops of the first phase — wheat, not corn, was the primary crop alongside rice.

 

• Cotton, indigo (Option 3): Incorrect; these were colonial-era cash crops, unrelated to the post-independence Green Revolution.

 

• Millet, wheat (Option 4): Incorrect; millets were not a major focus of the first phase — rice, not millet, was the paired staple crop.

question: As per physicists and their major contributions/discoveries,Which of the following pair is INCORRECT?
option_2: Louis Victor de Broglie – Wavenature of matter
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paul Dirac – Liquid helium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This pairing is INCORRECT: Paul Dirac is renowned for formulating the Dirac equation in quantum mechanics and predicting the existence of antimatter (the positron), not for work on liquid helium. (पॉल डिराक — क्वांटम यांत्रिकी, द्रव हीलियम नहीं)

 

• The phenomenon of superfluidity in liquid helium was discovered by Pyotr Kapitsa (1937) and theoretically explained by Lev Landau.

 

• Paul Dirac shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• John Bardeen won two Nobel Prizes in Physics — one for the invention of the transistor (1956) and another for the BCS theory of superconductivity (1972), along with Leon Cooper and John Schrieffer.

 

• Louis de Broglie proposed the concept of wave-particle duality of matter in his 1924 doctoral thesis, for which he won the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physics.

 

NOTE

 

• John Bardeen – Theory of superconductivity (Option 1): This pairing is correct; Bardeen co-developed the BCS theory of superconductivity.

 

• Louis Victor de Broglie – Wave nature of matter (Option 2): This pairing is correct; de Broglie proposed matter waves.

 

• Victor Francis Hess – Cosmic radiation (Option 3): This pairing is correct; Hess discovered cosmic rays in 1912, for which he won the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physics.

question: In December 2022, who among the following was elected as the first woman President of Indian Olympic Association?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PT Usha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary athlete PT Usha (Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha) was elected unopposed as the first woman President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in December 2022. (पी.टी. उषा — आईओए की पहली महिला अध्यक्ष)

 

• She took charge amid the IOA's efforts to reform its functioning following a period of administrative turmoil, ahead of India's bid to host future Olympic Games.

 

• PT Usha is a celebrated former sprinter, famously known as the "Payyoli Express", who narrowly missed a bronze medal by 1/100th of a second in the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PT Usha was also nominated as a Member of the Rajya Sabha in 2022.

 

• She had earlier been honoured with the Padma Shri (1985) and the Arjuna Award for her athletic achievements.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajlaxmi Singh Deo (Option 2): An Indian sports administrator associated with hockey, but not the IOA President elected in December 2022.

 

• Karnam Malleswari (Option 3): India's first woman Olympic medallist (weightlifting, Sydney 2000 Bronze), but not the IOA President elected in December 2022.

 

• Dola Banerjee (Option 4): A prominent Indian archer, but not the IOA President elected in December 2022.

question: What was the period of Harshavardhana's reign?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 606 CE to 647 CE.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harshavardhana, the last major ruler of ancient India before the age of regional kingdoms, ruled from 606 CE to 647 CE, with his capital at Kannauj (Kanyakubja). (हर्षवर्धन — 606-647 ईस्वी)

 

• He is known through the biography "Harshacharita", written by his court poet Banabhatta, and through the travel accounts of the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang), who visited his court.

 

• Harsha convened the famous Kannauj Assembly and the Prayag (Kumbh) Assembly, and was himself a playwright, authoring works such as Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Harsha was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II on the banks of the Narmada River, which checked his southward expansion.

 

• After Harsha's death in 647 CE without an heir, his empire disintegrated, marking the transition to a more fragmented political landscape in early medieval India.

 

NOTE

 

• 647 CE to 700 CE (Option 1): Incorrect; Harsha's reign actually ended (with his death) in 647 CE, not started then.

 

• 570 CE to 610 CE (Option 2): Incorrect; this period does not correspond to Harsha's established reign dates.

 

• 545 CE to 570 CE (Option 4): Incorrect; this predates Harsha's reign considerably.

question: Padma Bhushan awardee, Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, was a renowned guru for which of the following classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam was a legendary exponent and reformer of Kuchipudi, a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh. (कुचिपुड़ी — गुरु वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम)

 

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai in 1963, and is widely credited with transforming Kuchipudi from a temple/male-dominated dance-drama tradition into a structured solo classical dance form performed by both men and women.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in recognition of his immense contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kuchipudi derives its name from the village Kuchelapuram (Kuchipudi) in Andhra Pradesh's Krishna district, where it originated as a dance-drama tradition.

 

• Other renowned Kuchipudi exponents include Yamini Krishnamurthy and Raja and Radha Reddy.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): A classical dance form of Kerala, unrelated to Vempati Chinna Satyam.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A classical dance form of North India, associated with gurus like Birju Maharaj, not Vempati Chinna Satyam.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): A classical dance form of Odisha, associated with Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, not Vempati Chinna Satyam.

question: Famous dance personality Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which of these dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary exponent and one of the chief architects of the modern revival of Odissi, a classical dance form of Odisha. (ओडिसी — गुरु केलुचरण महापात्र)

 

• He trained numerous celebrated dancers, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi, and Madhavi Mudgal, significantly shaping the codified grammar of present-day Odissi.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (1988) for his contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi is characterised by its distinctive tribhangi (three-bend) posture and fluid, sculpturesque body movements inspired by temple sculptures of Odisha, particularly the Konark Sun Temple.

 

• The Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi and institutions like Srjan (founded by Kelucharan Mohapatra) continue to promote Odissi training today.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A North Indian classical dance form associated with gurus like Birju Maharaj, unrelated to Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 2): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, associated with gurus such as Rukmini Devi Arundale, not Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, unrelated to Kelucharan Mohapatra's contributions.

question: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire and contemporaries of this empire described it as the_______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka Samrajyamu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• While modern historians refer to the empire as the Vijayanagara Empire (after its capital city Vijayanagara), contemporaries of the empire, particularly in Telugu inscriptions, described it as the "Karnataka Samrajyamu" or "Karnataka Rajya". (कर्नाटक साम्राज्यमु — विजयनगर साम्राज्य का समकालीन नाम)

 

• The term "Karnataka" here was used in a broad historical-cultural sense referring to the region and its ruling dynasty's Kannada cultural sphere, rather than strictly the present-day state of Karnataka.

 

• The empire was founded in 1336 CE by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty, and reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire comprised four major dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

 

• The empire finally declined after its defeat at the Battle of Talikota (1565) against the combined Deccan Sultanates.

 

NOTE

 

• Gajapati Samarajya (Option 1): Refers to the Gajapati dynasty of Odisha, a contemporary but separate kingdom, not the term used for Vijayanagara.

 

• Andhra Samarajyu (Option 3): Not the historically attested contemporary term used for the Vijayanagara Empire.

 

• Sthalapati Samrajya (Option 4): Not a historically attested term associated with the Vijayanagara Empire.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 137.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 137 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review any judgement or order pronounced (or made) by it, subject to any law made by Parliament or rules made under Article 145. (अनुच्छेद 137 — सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की पुनर्विचार शक्ति)

 

• This provision is an exception to the general principle of finality of judgments, allowing the Supreme Court to correct errors that may have crept into its own earlier decisions.

 

• A review petition under Article 137 is generally decided by circulation among judges in their chambers, without oral arguments, unless the Court decides otherwise.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 137 falls under Part V of the Constitution, dealing with the Union Judiciary.

 

• Besides review, a curative petition (evolved through the 2002 Rupa Ashok Hurra case) is a further remedy available after a review petition is dismissed, to prevent abuse of process.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 138 (Option 1): Deals with the enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, not review of its own judgements.

 

• Article 135 (Option 2): Deals with the jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law being exercisable by the Supreme Court.

 

• Article 136 (Option 3): Grants the Supreme Court Special Leave to Appeal against any judgment/order of any court or tribunal in India, a different power from review of its own judgments.

question: For the political education of the people at the local level, who brought the resolution on local self-government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Ripon, Viceroy of India (1880-1884), brought the famous Resolution on Local Self-Government in 1882, aimed at providing political education to the people at the grassroots level. (लॉर्ड रिपन — स्थानीय स्वशासन का जनक)

 

• He is widely regarded as the "Father of Local Self-Government in India" for his efforts to establish and strengthen municipal boards and district boards with elected Indian representatives.

 

• His reforms aimed to train Indians in self-governance; he also repealed the controversial Vernacular Press Act and attempted to pass the Ilbert Bill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1992) later gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies, building on the foundations laid by Ripon's reforms.

 

• 24 April is celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day in India, commemorating the 73rd Amendment coming into force in 1993.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Mayo (Option 2): Viceroy (1869-1872) known for initiating financial decentralisation between the Centre and provinces, a precursor to but distinct from Ripon's local self-government resolution.

 

• Lord Canning (Option 3): The first Viceroy of India (1858-1862), associated with the aftermath of the 1857 revolt and the Indian Councils Act 1861, not local self-government.

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 4): Viceroy (1876-1880) known for repressive measures like the Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act, not local self-government reforms.

question: When was the International Day for Elder Persons 2021 celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 October.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day of Older Persons is observed every year on 1 October, as designated by the United Nations General Assembly in December 1990. (अंतरराष्ट्रीय वृद्धजन दिवस — 1 अक्टूबर)

 

• The day aims to raise awareness about issues affecting older persons, such as the ageing process, elder abuse, and the need to strengthen long-term and palliative care systems.

 

• In 2021, the theme for the day was "Digital Equity for All Ages", focusing on bridging the digital divide affecting elderly populations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The day was first observed in 1991, following the UN's adoption of the United Nations Principles for Older Persons in 1991.

 

• India also runs welfare initiatives for the elderly such as the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana.

 

NOTE

 

• 3 October, 4 October and 2 October (Options 2, 3 and 4): These dates are incorrect; the International Day of Older Persons is fixed by the UN General Assembly as 1 October every year, not any of these dates.

question: Which of the following elements has variable valency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iron (Fe) is a transition metal that exhibits variable valency, most commonly showing oxidation states of +2 (ferrous, Fe²⁺) and +3 (ferric, Fe³⁺). (परिवर्ती संयोजकता — लोहा)

 

• Variable valency in transition metals arises because electrons from both the outermost s-orbital and the penultimate d-orbital can participate in bond formation, allowing multiple stable oxidation states.

 

• Compounds like Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO₄) and Ferric Chloride (FeCl₃) illustrate iron's two common valencies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common elements with variable valency include Copper (Cu⁺/Cu²⁺), Mercury (Hg⁺/Hg²⁺), Lead (Pb²⁺/Pb⁴⁺), and Tin (Sn²⁺/Sn⁴⁺).

 

• Elements exhibiting only fixed valency, like alkali metals, generally form ionic bonds with a single stable oxidation state.

 

NOTE

 

• Sodium (Option 2): An alkali metal that shows a fixed valency of +1 only, due to having a single electron in its outermost shell.

 

• Sulphur (Option 3): In the basic school-level valency chart used for this classification, sulphur is treated as having a fixed normal valency of 2, unlike the classic multivalent (variable) nature of transition elements like iron.

 

• Magnesium (Option 4): An alkaline earth metal with a fixed valency of +2, due to its consistent loss of two electrons in bonding.

question: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded as a response to muslim fundamentalism in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1915.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 at Haridwar, during the Kumbh Mela, as a response to what its founders perceived as Muslim communalism and the formation of bodies like the All India Muslim League (1906). (हिंदू महासभा — 1915 में स्थापना)

 

• It was formally reorganised into an All-India body as the "Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha" in 1915, with leaders like Madan Mohan Malaviya playing key roles in its early years.

 

• The organisation later became prominent under leaders such as Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, who served as its president and propagated the ideology of Hindutva.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Muslim League was founded earlier, in 1906 at Dhaka, in reaction to which some Hindu nationalist organisations, including the Hindu Mahasabha, later emerged.

 

• The Hindu Mahasabha actively opposed the Congress's approach on several issues in the following decades of the freedom struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• 1917 (Option 1): Incorrect; this does not correspond to the founding year of the Hindu Mahasabha.

 

• 1925 (Option 3): Incorrect; 1925 is actually the founding year of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a different organisation, not the Hindu Mahasabha.

 

• 1910 (Option 4): Incorrect; this predates the actual founding of the Hindu Mahasabha in 1915.
